Test Description: Verify that exception list creation is captured in the audit trail with complete metadata.
Pre-Condition: User has permission to create an exception list and the action is performed successfully.
Test Steps: 1. Sign in with a role allowed to create exception lists. 2. Create a new list with valid name, category, and scope. 3. Save the record and wait for the confirmation banner. 4. Open the audit trail entry linked to the action. 5. Review the stored event details.
Expected Results: The audit log records the create event with timestamp, user details, object ID, and before/after state as applicable.

Test Description: Check that editing an exception list writes a new immutable audit event.
Pre-Condition: An existing exception list is available and the user updates at least one field.
Test Steps: 1. Open an active exception list. 2. Change one approved field such as description or expiry policy. 3. Submit the update and confirm the save message. 4. Open the audit history for the same list. 5. Compare the old and new values recorded in the log.
Expected Results: The edit action is written to the audit trail with both before-state and after-state snapshots.

Test Description: Validate that list suspension is recorded with the correct status change.
Pre-Condition: An active exception list exists and the user suspends it.
Test Steps: 1. Open the list detail page. 2. Choose the suspend action and confirm the prompt. 3. Finish the action and note the updated status. 4. Open the audit trail event for that list. 5. Verify the recorded change in status.
Expected Results: The audit trail stores the suspension event and shows the status transition from Active to Suspended.

Test Description: Confirm that re-activation of a list is logged as a separate event.
Pre-Condition: A suspended list is available and the user re-activates it.
Test Steps: 1. Locate a list that is currently suspended. 2. Select the re-activate option from the list actions. 3. Confirm the prompt and wait for the status to refresh. 4. Open the audit trail for the same object. 5. Check that the re-activation appears as its own event.
Expected Results: The audit trail contains a distinct re-activation record and does not overwrite the earlier suspension event.

Test Description: Verify that deleting an exception list leaves a permanent audit record.
Pre-Condition: A list exists with delete permission available to the user.
Test Steps: 1. Open the target list from the list view. 2. Trigger the delete action and confirm the warning dialog. 3. Complete the deletion flow. 4. Open the audit trail for the deleted object. 5. Check whether the event remains searchable after deletion.
Expected Results: The delete action is logged permanently and the audit record remains readable after the list is removed from active use.

Test Description: Ensure that exception entry submission is captured in the audit trail.
Pre-Condition: The user submits a new exception entry from the list screen.
Test Steps: 1. Open an exception list and start a new entry. 2. Fill in valid customer and watchlist details. 3. Add the required reason code and evidence reference. 4. Submit the entry into the approval flow. 5. Review the audit event created for the submission.
Expected Results: The audit trail stores the submission event with the entry ID, maker details, and submission timestamp.

Test Description: Check that approving an exception entry creates a separate audit trail record.
Pre-Condition: A pending maker-checker request is available for approval.
Test Steps: 1. Open the maker-checker queue. 2. Approve the pending exception entry using an authorised checker role. 3. Confirm the approval notification appears. 4. Open the audit trail and search for the same request ID. 5. Compare the approval details against the request screen.
Expected Results: The approval is stored as an independent audit event with the checker identity and approval outcome.

Test Description: Validate that rejection of an exception entry is written to the audit history.
Pre-Condition: A pending request is available and the checker rejects it.
Test Steps: 1. Open the pending request in the maker-checker queue. 2. Review the reason and evidence summary. 3. Reject the request with a short comment. 4. Open the audit trail for the request. 5. Verify the rejection state and comment are captured.
Expected Results: The audit log shows the rejected request, the checker comment, and the final decision status.

Test Description: Confirm that entry edit activity is tracked even when only a single field changes.
Pre-Condition: An existing exception entry is opened for editing.
Test Steps: 1. Open an approved entry from the list view. 2. Change only one editable field, such as expiry date or evidence reference. 3. Save the update. 4. Open the entry history or audit log. 5. Confirm the before-state and after-state differ only on the modified field.
Expected Results: The audit trail captures the edit at field level and preserves the previous values for review.

Test Description: Verify that entry suspension is logged when a user deactivates an approved entry.
Pre-Condition: An approved entry is active and the user suspends it.
Test Steps: 1. Open the active exception entry. 2. Select the suspend option from the action menu. 3. Confirm the prompt and complete the action. 4. Open the audit trail for the entry. 5. Check the event description and status change values.
Expected Results: The audit trail records the suspension event with the correct object ID and new status.

Test Description: Check that entry re-activation after suspension is audited separately from the original approval.
Pre-Condition: A suspended entry is made active again.
Test Steps: 1. Open the suspended entry. 2. Choose the re-activate action. 3. Confirm the action and wait for the status to update. 4. Open the audit trail for the same entry. 5. Verify the re-activation sits after the suspension in the event chain.
Expected Results: A new audit record is created for re-activation, and the old approval entry stays intact.

Test Description: Ensure that expired entries still remain visible in the audit trail after TTL passes.
Pre-Condition: An entry has already expired and screening suppression has ceased.
Test Steps: 1. Locate an entry whose expiry date is in the past. 2. Open the entry detail screen. 3. Navigate to its audit history. 4. Confirm the expiry event or state change is available. 5. Verify the record is still searchable after expiration.
Expected Results: The expired entry continues to appear in audit history and the expiry transition is retained.

Test Description: Validate that bulk upload submission creates a parent audit event.
Pre-Condition: A bulk upload file is prepared and submitted successfully.
Test Steps: 1. Open the bulk upload screen. 2. Upload a valid file containing multiple rows. 3. Submit the batch for processing. 4. Check the audit trail for the bulk action. 5. Confirm the parent event references the upload request ID.
Expected Results: The upload submission is written to the audit trail with a unique request reference.

Test Description: Confirm that bulk upload approval or rejection is recorded together with the batch outcome.
Pre-Condition: A bulk upload request is waiting in the maker-checker queue.
Test Steps: 1. Open the pending bulk upload request. 2. Approve or reject the batch from the checker account. 3. Note the final batch status shown on screen. 4. Open the corresponding audit trail entry. 5. Verify that the outcome matches the action taken.
Expected Results: The audit trail stores the batch decision and the final status of the upload request.

Test Description: Check that API submit, update, and delete events are logged with the caller identity.
Pre-Condition: An API client is configured with valid authentication and makes CSEL requests.
Test Steps: 1. Send a submit request through the API. 2. Update the same entry through another API call. 3. Delete or deactivate the record through the API. 4. Open the audit trail for each operation. 5. Compare the recorded user, IP, and object identifiers.
Expected Results: Each API action produces an audit event that includes the authenticated caller and operation type.

Test Description: Validate that every suppressed alert is logged silently without user-facing notification noise.
Pre-Condition: An active CSEL entry suppresses an incoming screening hit.
Test Steps: 1. Run a screening scenario that matches an approved entry. 2. Allow the engine to suppress the alert. 3. Check that no analyst-facing alert pop-up is shown for the suppression itself. 4. Open the audit trail and search for the suppression event. 5. Review the stored suppression identifiers.
Expected Results: The suppression is written to audit in real time, but the user interface does not raise a separate noisy notification.

Test Description: Confirm that suppression logging includes the watchlist, score, and screening timestamps.
Pre-Condition: A screening event is suppressed by an active CSEL entry.
Test Steps: 1. Open the customer screening event. 2. Note the watchlist name and match score on the alert. 3. Let the system apply the exception rule. 4. Open the audit trail entry for the suppression. 5. Verify the customer ID, entry ID, watchlist, score, and timestamps are present.
Expected Results: The audit record contains the full suppression ledger details required by the FSD.

Test Description: Check that evidence attachment upload is recorded in the audit trail.
Pre-Condition: The entry form allows an attachment and the file is uploaded successfully.
Test Steps: 1. Open an add or edit entry form. 2. Upload a valid evidence file. 3. Save the entry or draft. 4. Open the audit trail for that record. 5. Confirm the attachment action appears in history.
Expected Results: The audit trail captures the upload action with attachment reference and user details.

Test Description: Validate that viewing or downloading evidence is separately logged.
Pre-Condition: An evidence file already exists on an entry.
Test Steps: 1. Open the entry detail page. 2. View the attached evidence file. 3. Download the same file from the attachment control. 4. Open the audit trail for the entry. 5. Check that both view and download activities are present if the system tracks both.
Expected Results: The audit trail records access to the evidence attachment and preserves the action history.

Test Description: Ensure that a material identity change auto-suspension event is captured.
Pre-Condition: A customer record changes in a way that qualifies as a material identity change.
Test Steps: 1. Update a screened customer profile field such as name, DOB, or nationality. 2. Wait for the system to process the change. 3. Open the linked CSEL entry status. 4. Review the audit trail for the auto-suspension event. 5. Confirm the triggering change is identifiable.
Expected Results: The audit trail records the auto-suspension and links it to the underlying profile change.

Test Description: Verify that a true-hit conflict check blocked submission is recorded as an integrity event.
Pre-Condition: A customer ID already exists on an active custom blacklist.
Test Steps: 1. Start a new CSEL submission for the same customer. 2. Let the system run the conflict check. 3. Observe the submission block message. 4. Open the audit trail or integrity log. 5. Confirm the blocked event is recorded with the reason.
Expected Results: The blocked submission is written to audit as a conflict/integrity event rather than a normal approval.

Test Description: Confirm that the exception register report generation is logged.
Pre-Condition: The monthly report generation job or manual report request is executed.
Test Steps: 1. Open the reports area. 2. Generate the CSEL Exception Register report. 3. Wait for the file to finish processing. 4. Open the audit trail from the module. 5. Search for the report generation event and verify its metadata.
Expected Results: The audit trail records the report generation event with report type, user, and timestamp.

Test Description: Check that exporting the audit trail to CSV is itself logged.
Pre-Condition: The auditor or compliance user exports the audit trail data.
Test Steps: 1. Open the audit trail screen. 2. Apply a simple filter or keep the default view. 3. Choose the CSV export action. 4. Save the generated file locally. 5. Re-open the audit history and look for the export event.
Expected Results: The export action is written to audit, including format, user, and export time.

Test Description: Verify that audit records are read-only and cannot be edited through the application.
Pre-Condition: A user opens an existing audit record with full visibility.
Test Steps: 1. Search for an existing audit event. 2. Open the detail panel or row expansion. 3. Check whether any edit or delete action is exposed. 4. Try to navigate to a change path if the UI offers one. 5. Confirm that the record remains unchanged.
Expected Results: The application does not allow modification or deletion of the audit record.

Test Description: Ensure that audit records remain searchable after the retention period is configured.
Pre-Condition: Audit retention settings are in place and historical records are available.
Test Steps: 1. Search for an older audit event using a known object ID. 2. Apply date filters around the historical period. 3. Open the matching result. 4. Verify the event content is still visible. 5. Confirm the record is not hidden by ordinary application access rules.
Expected Results: Audit data remains available for the configured retention period and can still be retrieved for compliance review.

Test Description: Check that the audit trail shows before and after state snapshots for state-changing actions.
Pre-Condition: An action that changes record state is performed, such as edit or suspend.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger a state-changing event on a list or entry. 2. Open the audit detail for the same event. 3. Expand the JSON or state snapshot fields if available. 4. Compare the before and after values. 5. Confirm the changed fields are obvious from the log.
Expected Results: The audit trail contains both snapshots and clearly shows what changed during the action.

Test Description: Verify audit trail filters by event type, list, and date range per Figma.
Pre-Condition: Mixed audit events exist.
Test Steps: 1. Open Audit trail. 2. Filter by event type. 3. Filter by list. 4. Set date range. 5. Confirm results.
Expected Results: Filters narrow results correctly and can be combined.

Test Description: Verify Read-Only Auditor has read/export access only on audit trail.
Pre-Condition: Auditor account available.
Test Steps: 1. Login as Auditor. 2. Open audit trail. 3. View events. 4. Export. 5. Confirm no edit/delete.
Expected Results: Auditor can read/export but cannot modify audit records.

Test Description: Verify MLRO and Compliance Manager have full read access to all audit records.
Pre-Condition: Audit events from multiple makers exist.
Test Steps: 1. Login as MLRO. 2. Open audit trail. 3. Search events from other users. 4. Repeat as Compliance Manager. 5. Confirm full visibility.
Expected Results: MLRO and Compliance Manager can view all audit records regardless of maker.

Test Description: Verify non-privileged roles see only audit records related to their own submissions.
Pre-Condition: KYC Analyst with own and others' submissions in system.
Test Steps: 1. Login as KYC Analyst. 2. Open audit trail. 3. Search own submission events — visible. 4. Search other user's events. 5. Confirm restricted.
Expected Results: Restricted roles see only own-submission related audit records.

Test Description: Check that a new exception entry cannot be submitted when any mandatory field is left blank.
Pre-Condition: User is logged in with permission to add entries and a target exception list is open.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Add Exception Entry form from the selected list. 2. Leave Customer ID and Date of Birth empty, but complete the other visible fields. 3. Try to submit the form once to trigger validation. 4. Fill one missing field and leave another required field blank. 5. Submit again and observe the response.
Expected Results: The form blocks submission, highlights every missing mandatory field, and does not move the record to the approval queue.

Test Description: Verify the conditional behaviour for Original Script Name and Script Type when a non-Latin name is entered.
Pre-Condition: The add-entry screen is open and the customer name is available in a native script such as Arabic or Cyrillic.
Test Steps: 1. Enter the customer name in the Original Script Name field. 2. Skip the Script Type / Language field and keep the rest of the form valid. 3. Try to continue to submission. 4. Add the matching script type value and submit the same record again. 5. Review whether the saved record keeps the UTF-8 text intact.
Expected Results: The system requires Script Type when Original Script Name is populated, accepts the entry only after it is completed, and stores the native-script text correctly.

Test Description: Create a fresh exception entry from the list screen and confirm that it goes through maker-checker approval.
Pre-Condition: A compliance user can access an active exception list and no duplicate entry already exists for the same customer and watchlist.
Test Steps: 1. Open the selected exception list. 2. Click Add Entry from the list actions. 3. Populate the customer, watchlist, reason code, expiry date, and distinguishing attributes. 4. Attach the supporting evidence file before submission. 5. Submit the request and check the request status in the queue.
Expected Results: The entry is accepted, saved as Pending Approval, and becomes visible in the maker-checker workflow instead of going active immediately.

Test Description: Use the alert-driven path and verify that the entry form is prefilled from the screening alert.
Pre-Condition: A screening alert exists for the same customer and the user opens it from the alert management screen.
Test Steps: 1. Open the alert detail page for a false-positive hit. 2. Choose Add to Exception List from the alert actions. 3. Check the form fields that should be copied from the alert. 4. Compare Screening Date, Alert Reference ID, Matched Watchlist Entry, Match Score, and Watchlist Name with the source alert. 5. Complete the remaining fields and submit the entry.
Expected Results: The prefilled fields match the alert record, reducing manual entry, and the submission follows the standard approval flow.

Test Description: Block the submission when the customer is already present on an active Custom List or blacklist.
Pre-Condition: The add-entry screen is open and the Customer ID being tested exists on an active custom blacklist.
Test Steps: 1. Type the conflicting Customer ID into the form. 2. Wait for the real-time conflict check to complete. 3. Observe the on-screen warning message. 4. Try to submit the entry anyway. 5. Confirm that the system keeps the request out of the approval queue.
Expected Results: The system stops the submission in real time, explains the conflict, and refuses to route the entry for approval.

Test Description: Check the warning path when the distinguishing evidence is too thin but the user chooses to continue.
Pre-Condition: The analyst is creating an exception entry and the evidence section is not fully populated.
Test Steps: 1. Enter the base customer and watchlist details. 2. Leave the Distinguishing Attributes field very short or almost empty. 3. Review the warning banner shown by the system. 4. Confirm that sufficient evidence is available. 5. Submit the record and inspect the submission outcome.
Expected Results: A non-blocking warning appears, the user must confirm the evidence is adequate, and the request can still proceed to approval.

Test Description: Update an approved entry and verify that the change is sent back through the approval workflow.
Pre-Condition: An active entry exists and the user has edit permission for that record.
Test Steps: 1. Open the entry details from the list view. 2. Select Edit and change a non-destructive field such as expiry date or reason detail. 3. Save the update and capture the confirmation message. 4. Open the approval queue or refresh the entry status. 5. Check the view history to confirm the old and new values are both retained.
Expected Results: The edit is not applied silently, the request is submitted for approval, and the history trail shows the before-and-after values.

Test Description: Make sure an entry sitting in Pending Approval cannot be edited until the request is resolved.
Pre-Condition: The target entry already has an open approval request and is not yet active.
Test Steps: 1. Open the pending entry from the list or queue. 2. Click Edit on the same record. 3. Try to change one visible field. 4. Attempt to save the change. 5. Check the status message or disabled state shown by the screen.
Expected Results: The edit action is blocked while the record is Pending Approval, so no new version is created until the first request is completed.

Test Description: Validate that scope expansion sends the edit to a higher approval level than a simple reduction.
Pre-Condition: The entry is active and the test user can initiate an edit on it.
Test Steps: 1. Open the record and choose Edit. 2. Add another watchlist to the scope or extend the expiry date beyond the original value. 3. Enter the change reason and submit the request. 4. Open the maker-checker queue for the item. 5. Check the assigned checker role before approval is allowed.
Expected Results: The expanded edit is routed to the stricter Compliance Officer or Compliance Manager approval path instead of the standard level.

Test Description: Suspend a live entry and confirm that suppression stops as soon as the approval is completed.
Pre-Condition: An active entry is currently suppressing a known false positive.
Test Steps: 1. Open the entry actions from the list detail view. 2. Choose Suspend and provide the required reason. 3. Submit the request and complete approval. 4. Run the same customer through screening again. 5. Compare the alert behaviour before and after the suspension.
Expected Results: After approval, the entry is excluded from evaluation, suppression ceases immediately, and the alert is raised again on screening.

Test Description: Soft-delete an entry and verify that the system keeps the record for audit and history review.
Pre-Condition: The entry exists in active or suspended state and the user has permission to request deletion.
Test Steps: 1. Open the entry and choose Delete. 2. Enter the mandatory deletion reason. 3. Send the request through the approval flow. 4. Search for the same entry after approval. 5. Open the audit or history view to confirm the retained record.
Expected Results: The entry is marked Deleted rather than physically removed, and the system still exposes the record in audit and history views.

Test Description: Verify that the pre-expiry reminder workflow fires before the TTL runs out.
Pre-Condition: A test entry is configured with an expiry date close enough to trigger the reminder window.
Test Steps: 1. Set or select an entry that is due to expire within the test window. 2. Wait for the 30-day reminder trigger or simulate the scheduled job. 3. Check the in-app notification for the list owner and Compliance Officer. 4. Move the scenario forward to the 7-day escalation point. 5. Confirm that the second reminder appears as well.
Expected Results: The system sends the first reminder at 30 days, escalates again at 7 days, and records the notifications for the relevant users.

Test Description: Confirm that an entry flips to Expired automatically and no longer suppresses matches once TTL has passed.
Pre-Condition: A valid entry is available with a controlled expiry time that can be crossed during the test.
Test Steps: 1. Note the current status of the active entry. 2. Advance the system clock or wait until the expiry time is reached. 3. Refresh the entry screen after the 5-minute expiry window. 4. Screen the same customer again against the watchlist. 5. Check the resulting alert status.
Expected Results: The entry becomes Expired automatically, suppression stops, and the alert is allowed to reappear on the next screening run.

Test Description: Renew an expired entry and ensure the new request follows the standard approval cycle.
Pre-Condition: An entry has already expired and is visible in the list detail screen.
Test Steps: 1. Open the expired record. 2. Click Renew from the entry actions. 3. Update the TTL or supporting evidence if the screen requests it. 4. Submit the renewal request. 5. Check whether the renewed record appears as a fresh approval item or a new active entry after approval.
Expected Results: Renewal creates a new approval event, and the entry only becomes active again after the renewal request is approved.

Test Description: Upload a clean CSV batch and verify that the import reaches the approval stage with the correct summary.
Pre-Condition: The bulk-upload template is available and the test file contains only valid rows.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Bulk Upload option from the list view. 2. Download the template and populate it with valid exception rows. 3. Upload the completed file. 4. Review the parsing summary shown by the system. 5. Submit the batch and check the queue status.
Expected Results: The file is accepted, the valid rows are counted correctly, and the batch moves forward in maker-checker rather than failing at upload time.

Test Description: Check how the system handles a mixed file that contains both valid and invalid rows.
Pre-Condition: A bulk file has a few good rows and at least one row with a missing or malformed mandatory field.
Test Steps: 1. Upload the mixed CSV through Bulk Upload. 2. Open the validation summary after parsing finishes. 3. Read the row-level error messages for the bad records. 4. Export or download the error log if the screen offers it. 5. Confirm whether the valid rows are separated clearly from the rejected ones.
Expected Results: The system presents row-level validation detail, points out the bad records, and does not let the poor-quality rows pass unnoticed.

Test Description: Verify that create, update, and delete actions received through API calls are captured in the audit trail.
Pre-Condition: An API client is authorised to sync exception entries into the module.
Test Steps: 1. Send a create request for a new exception entry. 2. Follow it with an update request on the same record. 3. Send a delete request for that entry. 4. Open the audit trail and filter for API sync activity. 5. Compare the object IDs, timestamps, and event types with the requests you sent.
Expected Results: Each API action is recorded as a distinct sync event, and the audit trail shows the full create-update-delete sequence.

Test Description: Push the API request rate past the configured limit and confirm that throttling kicks in.
Pre-Condition: A test client can generate a controlled burst of exception-submission requests.
Test Steps: 1. Start a short load test against the exception submission endpoint. 2. Increase the request volume until it crosses the steady-state limit. 3. Keep sending requests through the burst window. 4. Watch for the first throttled or rejected response. 5. Check the HTTP status or error message returned by the API.
Expected Results: The API starts throttling once the limit is crossed, and excess requests are rejected instead of being processed normally.

Test Description: Verify that a partially completed exception entry can be saved as Draft without entering the approval workflow.
Pre-Condition: User has permission to create exception entries and Add Entry screen is open.
Test Steps: 1. Open Add Entry screen. 2. Enter partial information. 3. Click Save Draft. 4. Reopen the Draft entry. 5. Verify saved values.
Expected Results: Entry is saved successfully in Draft status and does not appear in the Pending Approval queue.

Test Description: Verify that a Draft with missing mandatory fields cannot be submitted for approval.
Pre-Condition: Draft entry exists with missing mandatory fields.
Test Steps: 1. Open Draft. 2. Leave mandatory fields blank. 3. Click Submit. 4. Observe validation messages. 5. Verify workflow status.
Expected Results: Submission is blocked, validation messages are displayed, and the draft remains unsubmitted.

Test Description: Verify that a saved Draft can be edited and updated values are retained.
Pre-Condition: Draft entry already exists.
Test Steps: 1. Open Draft. 2. Modify editable fields. 3. Save Draft again. 4. Reopen Draft. 5. Verify updated values.
Expected Results: Modified values are retained successfully and status remains Draft.

Test Description: Verify that invalid updates in Draft prevent successful submission.
Pre-Condition: Draft entry exists.
Test Steps: 1. Open Draft. 2. Remove a mandatory field value. 3. Click Submit. 4. Observe validation. 5. Verify workflow status.
Expected Results: System displays validation errors and prevents submission.

Test Description: Verify that a completed Draft can be submitted and routed to Maker-Checker approval.
Pre-Condition: Draft contains all valid mandatory data.
Test Steps: 1. Open Draft. 2. Complete all mandatory fields. 3. Click Submit. 4. Open approval queue. 5. Verify request status.
Expected Results: Draft status changes to Pending Approval and request appears in Maker-Checker queue.

Test Description: Verify IP Address/CIDR and IP Validity Period validate for IP Range exception type.
Pre-Condition: Add entry form is open.
Test Steps: 1. Select IP Range type. 2. Enter valid CIDR and 90-day validity. 3. Submit. 4. Retry with 91 days. 5. Retry without IP address.
Expected Results: IP fields required for IP Range; validity accepts 1–90 days and rejects above 90.

Test Description: Verify Mobile Number enforces E.164 format when exception type is Mobile Number.
Pre-Condition: Add entry form is open.
Test Steps: 1. Select Mobile Number type. 2. Enter invalid format. 3. Attempt submit. 4. Enter valid E.164. 5. Complete and submit.
Expected Results: Invalid formats rejected; valid E.164 accepted.

Test Description: Verify Reason Detail enforces minimum 50 and maximum 2,000 characters.
Pre-Condition: Add entry form open with other mandatory fields completed.
Test Steps: 1. Enter 49 chars and submit. 2. Enter 50 chars and submit. 3. Enter 2,001 chars. 4. Observe validation. 5. Submit with 2,000 chars.
Expected Results: Reason Detail outside 50–2,000 range is rejected; valid range allows submission.

Test Description: Verify Other reason code requires 200+ chars in Reason Detail and MLRO checker routing.
Pre-Condition: Maker creating entry with Other reason code.
Test Steps: 1. Select Other. 2. Enter under 200 chars and submit. 3. Enter 200+ chars and submit. 4. Open maker-checker queue. 5. Verify MLRO required.
Expected Results: Blocked below 200 chars; valid Other entries route to MLRO.

Test Description: Verify checker requirement hint on entry form per Figma (CO/CM vs MLRO).
Pre-Condition: Add entry form is open.
Test Steps: 1. Review governance hint. 2. Select PEP reason code. 3. Confirm MLRO indicated. 4. Select standard code. 5. Confirm CO/CM requirement.
Expected Results: Form displays correct checker guidance for standard vs PEP/Other entries.

Test Description: Verify Re-activate for suspended entries routes through maker-checker with mandatory reason.
Pre-Condition: Suspended exception entry exists.
Test Steps: 1. Open suspended entry. 2. Select Re-activate. 3. Enter mandatory reason. 4. Submit. 5. After approval verify Active status.
Expected Results: Re-activate requires approval and restores Active status after checker approval.

Test Description: Verify Renew on expired entry creates new approval submission.
Pre-Condition: Expired entry in list detail.
Test Steps: 1. Open expired entry. 2. Click Renew. 3. Update TTL and evidence. 4. Submit. 5. Verify new MC request.
Expected Results: Renewal creates new approval request; active only after checker approval.

Test Description: Verify material identity change auto-suspends entries within 15 minutes.
Pre-Condition: Customer has active CSEL entries.
Test Steps: 1. Note active status. 2. Change name/DOB/nationality in core banking. 3. Wait up to 15 min. 4. Refresh entry status. 5. Check CO notification.
Expected Results: Entries auto-suspended within 15 minutes; Compliance Officer notified.

Test Description: Verify bulk upload duplicate detection for same customer ID and watchlist scope.
Pre-Condition: Bulk file with duplicate rows prepared.
Test Steps: 1. Upload file with duplicates. 2. Run validation. 3. Review error report. 4. Confirm duplicates flagged. 5. Submit unique rows only.
Expected Results: Duplicates identified in validation and excluded until resolved.

Test Description: Verify checker can drill into bulk upload rows before batch approval.
Pre-Condition: Bulk upload pending in MC queue.
Test Steps: 1. Open bulk request. 2. Drill into row detail. 3. Review fields. 4. Approve batch. 5. Confirm rows activate.
Expected Results: Checker inspects row detail before approval; valid rows activate.

Test Description: Verify View History panel shows submission, approval, and suppression events per Figma.
Pre-Condition: Entry with history exists.
Test Steps: 1. Click View History. 2. Expand items. 3. Verify submitted/approved/suppressed events. 4. Compare timestamps. 5. Close panel.
Expected Results: History panel shows chronological expandable events matching audit.

Test Description: Verify match score colour-coded badge in entry grid per Figma.
Pre-Condition: Entries with varied scores exist.
Test Steps: 1. Open entry grid. 2. Check high (≥90), medium, low scores. 3. Verify colour bands. 4. Refresh page. 5. Confirm consistency.
Expected Results: Score badges use distinct colours for high, medium, and low per Figma.

Test Description: Verify POST /csel/conflict-check blocks conflicting customer ID before submission.
Pre-Condition: API client authorized; customer on custom blacklist.
Test Steps: 1. Call conflict-check. 2. Review response. 3. Attempt POST entry. 4. Verify blocked. 5. Check integrity audit event.
Expected Results: Conflict-check flags conflict; submission blocked and logged.

Test Description: Verify API bulk endpoint accepts up to 500 entries per call.
Pre-Condition: API bulk access available.
Test Steps: 1. Submit 500 entries. 2. Confirm acceptance. 3. Submit 501. 4. Review error. 5. Verify excess not queued.
Expected Results: 500 accepted; 501 rejected with clear limit error.

Test Description: Verify KYC onboarding flagged Pending CSEL Approval on onboarding exception submit.
Pre-Condition: Customer in active KYC onboarding flow.
Test Steps: 1. Submit onboarding exception. 2. Open KYC queue. 3. Verify pending flag. 4. Approve exception. 5. Verify flag clears per policy.
Expected Results: KYC shows Pending CSEL Approval until checker approves (or conditional release).

Test Description: Verify Script Type values AR, ZH-CN, ZH-TW, CY, LA per FSD.
Pre-Condition: Original script name populated.
Test Steps: 1. Enter Original Script Name. 2. Open Script Type dropdown. 3. Verify FSD values. 4. Save draft. 5. Reopen and confirm.
Expected Results: Script Type contains all FSD values and persists correctly.

Test Description: Verify bulk suspend/delete of multiple entries is not supported per FSD.
Pre-Condition: List with multiple active entries.
Test Steps: 1. Attempt multi-select suspend/delete. 2. Confirm only single-entry actions available. 3. Process one entry. 4. Verify MC flow. 5. Confirm no bulk path.
Expected Results: Bulk suspend/delete unavailable; each entry actioned individually.

Test Description: Verify Jurisdiction Scope optional field limits exception application to specified jurisdiction when populated.
Pre-Condition: Add entry form is open.
Test Steps: 1. Create entry with jurisdiction scope set to a specific country. 2. Submit and approve. 3. Screen customer from matching jurisdiction — verify suppression. 4. Screen same customer from different jurisdiction — verify alert fires. 5. Check audit log.
Expected Results: Exception applies only within configured jurisdiction scope.

Test Description: Verify Email Address conditional field validates format when alert was triggered by email match.
Pre-Condition: Add entry form supports email-based exception type.
Test Steps: 1. Select exception context requiring email. 2. Enter invalid email format. 3. Attempt submit. 4. Enter valid email. 5. Complete mandatory fields and submit.
Expected Results: Invalid email rejected; valid email stored and submission proceeds to approval queue.

Test Description: Verify True Hit confirmed alert cannot be submitted to CSEL per FSD scope.
Pre-Condition: Screening alert confirmed as True Hit in case management.
Test Steps: 1. Open confirmed True Hit alert. 2. Attempt Add to Exception List. 3. Observe system response. 4. Verify no MC request created. 5. Check audit/integrity log if blocked.
Expected Results: True Hit cannot be added to CSEL; submission is blocked with clear message.

Test Description: Verify entry can be initiated from Case Management with evidence reference linked to source case.
Pre-Condition: Active case record exists in Case Management.
Test Steps: 1. Open case record. 2. Initiate CSEL entry from case. 3. Verify evidence reference pre-linked. 4. Complete and submit. 5. Open case link from entry detail.
Expected Results: Entry initiated from case with valid cross-reference to source case.

Test Description: Verify Download Template from bulk upload returns XLSX with all mandatory columns per FSD.
Pre-Condition: User has bulk upload access on list detail.
Test Steps: 1. Open Bulk Upload panel. 2. Click Download Template. 3. Open XLSX file. 4. Verify mandatory column headers. 5. Compare against FSD column specification.
Expected Results: Template contains all mandatory FSD columns with correct header names.

Test Description: Verify GET /csel/{listId}/entries returns paginated filtered results for API client.
Pre-Condition: API client authorized; list contains multiple entries.
Test Steps: 1. Call GET entries with pagination params. 2. Apply status filter. 3. Verify response page size. 4. Apply search term. 5. Compare with UI list data.
Expected Results: GET endpoint returns correct paginated, filtered entry data.

Test Description: Verify GET /csel/{listId}/entries/{entryId}/audit returns full entry audit history.
Pre-Condition: Entry with multiple audit events exists.
Test Steps: 1. Call GET audit endpoint for entry. 2. Compare events with UI audit trail. 3. Verify timestamps and event types. 4. Check before/after snapshots if returned. 5. Confirm completeness.
Expected Results: API returns complete audit history matching UI audit records.

Test Description: Verify exception list landing page opens with updated summary cards (Total lists, Active lists, Total exceptions, Pending approval), status tabs, list grid columns (including Exp 30d/Expired), and row actions per FSD v1.1 and Figma v3.
Pre-Condition: User is logged in with CSEL view access and the exception list index contains active data.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Exception lists menu from the left navigation. 2. Wait for the landing page to render completely. 3. Check the summary counters at the top of the screen. 4. Scan the list grid for the expected columns and row actions. 5. Confirm that search, filters, sorting, pagination, and export controls are visible.
Expected Results: The landing page loads successfully, the summary cards display values, and the grid shows the required columns and actions without layout issues.

Test Description: Check that list search, filter, sort, pagination, and file export behave as a single flow on the landing screen.
Pre-Condition: User is on the landing page and at least 11 exception lists exist so paging can be tested.
Test Steps: 1. Type a known list name into the search box and note the result count. 2. Clear the search and apply a category filter, then add a status filter on top of it. 3. Click a column header such as Total Entries to change the sort order. 4. Switch the page size from 10 to 25 and move to the next page. 5. Export the current view as CSV and then as PDF.
Expected Results: The grid refreshes according to the selected search and filters, sorting changes the row order, pagination updates the page set, and both export formats download the same filtered dataset.

Test Description: Create a new exception list with valid input and verify that it is routed through the approval flow.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is available and the list name does not already exist.
Test Steps: 1. Click CREATE NEW LIST from the landing page. 2. Enter a fresh list name, choose a category, and write a short purpose. 3. Fill in the default expiry period, default review frequency, and creation reason. 4. Submit the form and wait for the system response. 5. Re-open the list from the queue or the landing page if it appears there.
Expected Results: The list is accepted, saved with the submitted values, and placed into maker-checker approval instead of being activated immediately.

Test Description: Confirm that mandatory fields and duplicate list names are blocked at save time.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is on the create form and an existing list name is already available for reuse in the test.
Test Steps: 1. Open the create form again from the landing page. 2. Leave the required fields empty and try to continue once. 3. Enter a duplicate list name and keep the other fields valid. 4. Push one field beyond its allowed length, such as the name or purpose. 5. Attempt to submit the form after each check.
Expected Results: The form refuses submission, inline validation appears for missing or oversized data, and duplicate list names are not accepted.

Test Description: Validate the PEP exception list rule that the default review frequency cannot exceed six months.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is creating a new list under the PEP Exceptions category.
Test Steps: 1. Start a new list creation. 2. Select PEP Exceptions as the category. 3. Set the default review frequency to 12 months. 4. Keep the remaining fields valid and try to submit. 5. Change the frequency to 6 months and submit again.
Expected Results: The first submission is rejected with a business-rule message, while the corrected six-month setup can move forward in the approval workflow.

Test Description: Open a list in view mode and confirm that the metadata and entry sections match the FSD layout.
Pre-Condition: User has access to at least one existing exception list with linked entries.
Test Steps: 1. From the landing page, click View for a specific list. 2. Read the metadata block at the top of the page. 3. Scroll to the exception entry records section. 4. Verify the visible columns, status labels, and action links. 5. Check that the search, filter, sort, and export controls are present for entry records.
Expected Results: The view page shows the list metadata, summary counts, and entry grid fields exactly as defined, with no missing action controls.

Test Description: Validate entry-level search, filter, sort, and export from the list detail screen.
Pre-Condition: The selected list has entries in different statuses, expiry dates, and watchlist scopes.
Test Steps: 1. Open the list detail page. 2. Filter the entry grid by status and then by expiry date. 3. Narrow the rows by watchlist and reason code. 4. Click one of the sortable columns to change the order. 5. Export the record set to CSV and PDF.
Expected Results: The entry table refreshes correctly after every filter, the sort order changes as requested, and the exported files contain the same filtered record set.

Test Description: Change the allowed fields of an existing list and send the update through approval.
Pre-Condition: Maker user has edit permission on an active list.
Test Steps: 1. Open the list and choose Edit. 2. Update the list name or purpose, then adjust the default TTL and review frequency. 3. Add a reason for the change when prompted. 4. Save the update and wait for the system to respond. 5. Revisit the list from the queue or the list view to confirm the new state.
Expected Results: The modified values are captured, the request is routed for approval, and the system records the edit instead of applying it silently.

Test Description: Check that the list category stays locked after creation and cannot be changed during edit.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is editing an existing list that already has a fixed category.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Edit screen for the target list. 2. Locate the List Category field on the form. 3. Try to change it from the dropdown or keyboard. 4. Review the rest of the editable fields and press Save. 5. Watch for any validation or blocked-field message.
Expected Results: The category remains read-only or blocked, the edit request cannot change that field, and only the allowed fields stay editable.

Test Description: Suspend a list and verify that the system warns the user before the action is committed.
Pre-Condition: Authorized user can place the list into suspension and the list is currently active.
Test Steps: 1. Open the target list from the landing page. 2. Choose the Suspend action. 3. Read the warning about the screening impact and confirm the action. 4. Complete the approval step if the workflow sends it to maker-checker. 5. Refresh the page and check the list status.
Expected Results: The system shows the risk warning, the suspension request is recorded, and the list status changes to Suspended only after the action is completed.

Test Description: Bring back a suspended list and confirm that the earlier active entries return to use.
Pre-Condition: The selected list is already suspended and the user has permission to re-activate it.
Test Steps: 1. Open the suspended list. 2. Click the Re-activate option. 3. Confirm the prompt and submit the request. 4. Complete approval if the workflow requires it. 5. Reopen the list and check the status of the affected entries.
Expected Results: The list returns to Active, previously active entries are restored to the screening path, and the suppression behaviour is applied again.

Test Description: Delete a list through the supported soft-delete flow and verify that the reason is mandatory.
Pre-Condition: User has delete permission on the target list and maker-checker approval is enabled.
Test Steps: 1. Pick a list from the landing page and select Delete. 2. Enter the required deletion reason. 3. Submit the request and wait for the approval handoff. 4. Open the queue or revisit the list after approval. 5. Check whether the list still appears in the active index.
Expected Results: The delete request cannot go through without a reason, and after approval the list is removed from the active index rather than being permanently erased.

Test Description: Confirm that deleted lists are retained as soft-deleted records and are not physically purged.
Pre-Condition: A list has already been deleted through the approved workflow.
Test Steps: 1. Search for the deleted list from the landing page. 2. Open the audit or history view for the same list if available. 3. Check whether the deleted record is still retained in the system. 4. Try to reopen the list from the active listing. 5. Verify the retention status or system message shown for the record.
Expected Results: The deleted list is not returned in the active landing page, the record remains traceable as a retained item, and physical deletion is not allowed.

Test Description: Verify that landing page counters recalculate correctly after entry status changes.
Pre-Condition: Landing page contains exception lists with active entries.
Test Steps: 1. Note current counter values. 2. Approve, suspend, expire, or renew an entry. 3. Refresh landing page. 4. Compare counters. 5. Verify updated counts.
Expected Results: Total Entries, Active, Expiring Within 30 Days, and Expired counters reflect the latest data accurately.

Test Description: Verify that dashboard counters update after approval and rejection actions.
Pre-Condition: Pending requests are available.
Test Steps: 1. Note dashboard counts. 2. Approve or reject a request. 3. Refresh page. 4. Review counters. 5. Compare values.
Expected Results: Dashboard values are recalculated immediately after workflow completion.

Test Description: Verify that dashboard counters remain consistent after page refresh and re-login.
Pre-Condition: Counters have recently changed due to system activity.
Test Steps: 1. Refresh page. 2. Logout. 3. Login again. 4. Open landing page. 5. Compare counts.
Expected Results: Dashboard displays the same recalculated values after refresh and new session login.

Test Description: Verify that List Name accepts exactly 100 characters.
Pre-Condition: User is on Create Exception List screen.
Test Steps: 1. Enter 100-character List Name. 2. Complete mandatory fields. 3. Submit form. 4. Observe response. 5. Verify creation.
Expected Results: System accepts the value and processes the request successfully.

Test Description: Verify that List Name exceeding 100 characters is rejected.
Pre-Condition: User is on Create Exception List screen.
Test Steps: 1. Enter 101-character List Name. 2. Complete mandatory fields. 3. Submit form. 4. Observe validation. 5. Verify error message.
Expected Results: System blocks submission and displays maximum length validation.

Test Description: Verify that Description accepts exactly 500 characters.
Pre-Condition: User is on Create Exception List screen.
Test Steps: 1. Enter 500-character Description. 2. Complete mandatory fields. 3. Submit form. 4. Observe response. 5. Verify creation.
Expected Results: System accepts the description and allows submission.

Test Description: Verify that Description exceeding 500 characters is rejected.
Pre-Condition: User is on Create Exception List screen.
Test Steps: 1. Enter 501-character Description. 2. Complete mandatory fields. 3. Submit form. 4. Observe validation. 5. Verify error message.
Expected Results: System blocks submission and displays maximum length validation message.

Test Description: Verify landing page summary cards display Total lists, Active lists, Total exceptions, and Pending approval per updated Figma.
Pre-Condition: User is logged in with CSEL view access and exception list data exists.
Test Steps: 1. Open Exception lists from the left navigation. 2. Verify the four summary cards at the top. 3. Compare each card value with underlying list and entry data. 4. Refresh the page. 5. Confirm values remain consistent.
Test Data: At least 5 active lists and 3 pending approval requests exist.
Expected Results: Summary cards show Total lists, Active lists, Total exceptions, and Pending approval with accurate counts.

Test Description: Verify list status tabs (Active, Suspended, All) filter the landing grid per updated Figma.
Pre-Condition: Landing page contains lists in Active and Suspended status.
Test Steps: 1. Open the landing page. 2. Click Active tab and note row count. 3. Click Suspended and verify only suspended lists appear. 4. Click All and verify combined count. 5. Confirm tab badges match filtered results.
Expected Results: Each status tab filters the grid correctly and badge counts match visible rows.

Test Description: Verify landing grid columns include Exp 30d and Expired entry counters per FSD and Figma.
Pre-Condition: Lists exist with entries expiring within 30 days and expired entries.
Test Steps: 1. Open landing page. 2. Inspect grid column headers. 3. Compare Exp 30d and Expired values for a known list. 4. Cross-check against list detail summary. 5. Export CSV and confirm columns.
Test Data: List with expiring and expired entries.
Expected Results: Grid shows Exp 30d and Expired columns aligned to list detail counts and export.

Test Description: Verify Create Exception List supports Save as draft without entering maker-checker queue.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is on the create list panel.
Test Steps: 1. Click Create new list. 2. Enter partial valid data. 3. Click Save as draft. 4. Reopen draft. 5. Verify it is not in pending approval queue.
Expected Results: Draft is saved, values retained on reopen, and no maker-checker request is created until Submit for approval.

Test Description: Verify Notify Compliance Officer and Auto-expire entries at TTL toggles persist on create form.
Pre-Condition: Maker user opens create list panel.
Test Steps: 1. Open create list form. 2. Toggle both options. 3. Complete mandatory fields and save draft. 4. Reopen draft. 5. Verify toggle states.
Expected Results: Toggles are visible, interactive, and saved values persist on draft reload.

Test Description: Verify Reason for Creation is mandatory and retained in audit log per FSD.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is on create list form.
Test Steps: 1. Complete all fields except Reason for Creation. 2. Attempt submit. 3. Enter reason and submit. 4. Open audit trail. 5. Confirm reason is recorded.
Test Data: Unique list name and valid category.
Expected Results: Submission blocked without reason; reason stored in audit log after submission.

Test Description: Verify 24 months default TTL option enforces MLRO sign-off requirement per FSD.
Pre-Condition: Maker user is creating a new list.
Test Steps: 1. Open create form. 2. Select 24 months (MLRO sign-off required). 3. Complete mandatory fields. 4. Submit for approval. 5. Verify MLRO checker routing.
Expected Results: 24-month TTL routes list creation to MLRO checker approval.

Test Description: Verify pagination supports 10, 25, 50, and 100 rows per page per FSD.
Pre-Condition: More than 100 exception lists exist or test data is seeded.
Test Steps: 1. Open landing page. 2. Set each page size option. 3. Count visible rows. 4. Navigate pages. 5. Confirm pager text updates.
Expected Results: All four page-size options work and pagination reflects selection.

Test Description: Verify Bulk upload is accessible from landing page header per updated Figma.
Pre-Condition: User has bulk upload permission.
Test Steps: 1. Open landing page. 2. Click Bulk upload in header. 3. Verify panel opens. 4. Confirm list selector and template download. 5. Close panel.
Expected Results: Bulk upload panel opens from landing header with required controls.

Test Description: Verify sidebar menu search filters navigation items per updated Figma shell.
Pre-Condition: User is logged into CSEL module.
Test Steps: 1. Type 'Maker' in sidebar search. 2. Verify Maker-checker remains visible. 3. Type 'Sanctions'. 4. Verify Screening items filter. 5. Clear search.
Expected Results: Sidebar search filters menu items in real time without breaking navigation.

Test Description: Verify that the report opens with the correct summary cards and section layout.
Pre-Condition: User has access to the Exception Register page and at least one report is available.
Test Steps: 1. Sign in with a role allowed to view reporting. 2. Open the Exception Register screen from the left menu. 3. Read the summary cards at the top of the page. 4. Check that the report sections load without any missing panel. 5. Confirm the page title matches the current reporting month.
Expected Results: The page loads with the expected summary cards, section headers, and the correct report title.

Test Description: Check that the total active exceptions count matches the data shown in the report table.
Pre-Condition: The register contains active lists and active entries for the selected month.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report for the current period. 2. Note the total active exceptions count from the summary card. 3. Compare it with the active rows visible in the register table. 4. Refresh the screen once more to rule out a stale value. 5. Verify the number remains consistent after reload.
Expected Results: The count shown on the summary card is aligned with the values represented in the report data.

Test Description: Validate the New This Month metric against newly created exception items.
Pre-Condition: At least one exception list or exception entry was created during the reporting month.
Test Steps: 1. Open the register report. 2. Locate the New This Month card. 3. Cross-check the figure against recently created exceptions in the system. 4. Open a recent record and confirm its creation date. 5. Ensure the record falls within the current reporting month.
Expected Results: The New This Month value reflects items created during the same calendar month as the report.

Test Description: Confirm that the Suppressions This Month metric increments when alerts are suppressed.
Pre-Condition: A valid active exception exists and at least one screening hit has been suppressed this month.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger a screening hit that should be suppressed by an approved exception. 2. Allow the engine to finish the suppression. 3. Return to the register report. 4. Read the Suppressions This Month card. 5. Compare the value with the suppression activity that just occurred.
Expected Results: The suppression counter updates and shows the current month’s suppression total.

Test Description: Check the Expiring Within 30 Days count and sample list entries.
Pre-Condition: Some exceptions are due to expire within 30 days.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Exception Register report. 2. Review the Expiring Within 30 Days summary card. 3. Scroll to the expiring items section. 4. Verify that the listed items show valid expiry dates. 5. Open one record and confirm the expiry date matches the warning bucket.
Expected Results: The warning count and the listed items both show entries that are genuinely close to expiry.

Test Description: Verify that the Entries by Reason Code breakdown is displayed with percentages.
Pre-Condition: The register has multiple reason-code categories in the current period.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report page. 2. Locate the Entries by Reason Code section. 3. Review each reason-code row and its percentage column. 4. Compare the visible split against the underlying register data. 5. Confirm that the total distribution looks complete and not truncated.
Expected Results: The reason-code breakdown renders correctly with counts and percentages for each category.

Test Description: Validate that clicking a reason code row opens the corresponding filtered view or detail context.
Pre-Condition: The report contains clickable reason-code rows.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Exception Register report. 2. Select one reason-code row from the list. 3. Observe whether the page opens a filtered list or a drill-down view. 4. Inspect the records returned by that selection. 5. Confirm the visible entries belong to the chosen reason code.
Expected Results: The selected reason code opens the related filtered context and shows matching records.

Test Description: Check that the watchlist analysis section shows the correct top watchlist sources.
Pre-Condition: The reporting month includes activity across several watchlists.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report page. 2. Move to the Watchlist Analysis section. 3. Read the top watchlists and their suppression or exception counts. 4. Compare them with known high-volume watchlists in the data. 5. Confirm that the ordering follows the displayed volume logic.
Expected Results: The watchlist analysis section lists the correct watchlist sources and the counts are shown in a sensible order.

Test Description: Confirm that the report export button creates a CSV file with the same visible data.
Pre-Condition: The user has export permission and the report contains at least one row.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report screen. 2. Keep the default filters or apply one simple filter. 3. Click Export CSV. 4. Download the generated file and open it. 5. Compare the exported rows with the values on screen.
Expected Results: The CSV export matches the visible report data and keeps the same key columns and row values.

Test Description: Confirm that the PDF export mirrors the report layout and includes the header information.
Pre-Condition: The report is available and the user can export PDFs.
Test Steps: 1. Open the register report. 2. Click Export PDF. 3. Save the document locally. 4. Open the PDF and inspect the first page. 5. Compare the title, summary numbers, and key sections against the UI.
Expected Results: The PDF export reflects the same report title, summary cards, and visible section structure.

Test Description: Verify that filters for list name or category narrow the report results correctly.
Pre-Condition: The report contains more than one list or category.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report page. 2. Use the search field or category dropdown. 3. Apply one filter value. 4. Observe the table and summary changes after the filter is applied. 5. Remove the filter and confirm the report returns to the default view.
Expected Results: Only the matching items remain visible after filtering, and the original view returns once the filter is cleared.

Test Description: Check that status filters return the expected list states such as Active or Suspended.
Pre-Condition: The register includes multiple list states.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Exception Register report. 2. Select the status filter. 3. Choose one state such as Active. 4. Review the rows shown after the filter is applied. 5. Switch to another state and compare the result set.
Expected Results: The table updates to show only records with the selected status.

Test Description: Validate the page-size control so the report shows the requested number of rows.
Pre-Condition: The report spans more rows than a single page can display.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report. 2. Change the page-size dropdown to a smaller value. 3. Observe the row count on the page. 4. Move to the next page and confirm pagination still works. 5. Change the page size back to the default setting.
Expected Results: The page displays the selected number of rows and pagination remains consistent.

Test Description: Confirm that pagination navigates between report pages without losing the selected filters.
Pre-Condition: The report has more than one page of data and a filter is already applied.
Test Steps: 1. Apply any valid filter to the report. 2. Move to the next page using the pagination control. 3. Review the records on the second page. 4. Return to the first page. 5. Check that the filter condition is still in effect.
Expected Results: Pagination works correctly and the active filter remains applied while moving across pages.

Test Description: Check that date-related values are displayed in the expected report format.
Pre-Condition: The register includes created dates, modified dates, and expiry dates.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report. 2. Read the date columns in the table. 3. Compare the displayed format with the application standard. 4. Open one record and inspect the same dates in the detail view. 5. Confirm the same date format is used across the module.
Expected Results: Dates are shown consistently in the expected format throughout the report.

Test Description: Validate that very long list names do not break the report layout.
Pre-Condition: At least one list or category has a long display name.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report with a long-name record present. 2. Locate the long label in the table or summary section. 3. Observe whether the text wraps, truncates, or overflows. 4. Resize the browser window if required. 5. Confirm that nearby rows remain readable.
Expected Results: The report layout remains stable and the long text is handled without visual corruption.

Test Description: Check that special characters and punctuation in list names are rendered safely.
Pre-Condition: A report row contains characters such as ampersands, apostrophes, or hyphens.
Test Steps: 1. Open the register report. 2. Find a row with punctuation in its label. 3. Inspect the rendered text on screen. 4. Export the report to CSV or PDF. 5. Confirm the same text remains readable in the exported file.
Expected Results: Special characters display correctly and are not mangled in the UI or exported output.

Test Description: Confirm that the report handles an empty result set with a proper no-data message.
Pre-Condition: A filter combination returns no matching records.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report page. 2. Apply a restrictive filter set. 3. Search for a combination that yields no rows. 4. Observe the table area after submission. 5. Clear the filters to return to the normal report view.
Expected Results: The screen shows a clear no-data state rather than a blank or broken grid.

Test Description: Verify that a user without report permission cannot export or view the register data.
Pre-Condition: A restricted role account is available.
Test Steps: 1. Log in with a low-privilege account. 2. Try opening the Exception Register page. 3. Attempt to use export actions or drill-down links. 4. Note any permission warning or blocked control. 5. Sign in with an authorised role and compare the available actions.
Expected Results: Restricted users cannot access or export the report, while authorised users can.

Test Description: Check that the report refreshes to show recent screening activity after new events occur.
Pre-Condition: A new exception or suppression event has just been generated.
Test Steps: 1. Record the current value of a visible counter. 2. Trigger a new qualifying screening event. 3. Return to the report after the system finishes processing. 4. Refresh the page. 5. Verify the counter or related summary metric has updated.
Expected Results: The report reflects recent activity after refresh and does not keep an outdated snapshot.

Test Description: Validate that report values are consistent across screen refresh and browser reopen.
Pre-Condition: The register page has already loaded once successfully.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report and note the visible metrics. 2. Refresh the browser tab. 3. Compare the numbers after reload. 4. Close the tab and open the report again. 5. Confirm the same data set is returned for the same reporting period.
Expected Results: The report remains stable across refresh and reopen actions for the same period.

Test Description: Check that the report summary does not mix current month and historical month totals.
Pre-Condition: Historical data exists for previous months and the month selector is available.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report for the current month. 2. Switch to a previous month. 3. Review the summary counts and section totals. 4. Switch back to the current month. 5. Compare whether the numbers change with the selected period only.
Expected Results: Each selected month shows its own totals and does not leak values from another period.

Test Description: Confirm that the report can be opened without visible performance lag on a normal dataset.
Pre-Condition: A standard-sized register dataset is available.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Exception Register page. 2. Measure the time until the summary cards appear. 3. Wait for the tables and analytics sections to finish rendering. 4. Scroll through the visible content once loaded. 5. Note whether the page remains responsive during navigation.
Expected Results: The report loads within an acceptable time and remains responsive on a standard dataset.

Test Description: Verify that the report header shows the correct month label and delivery context.
Pre-Condition: The reporting engine has generated the current period output.
Test Steps: 1. Open the Exception Register page. 2. Read the month label shown in the report header. 3. Compare it with the current generation period. 4. Confirm the delivery note or subtitle is visible if present. 5. Reopen the page to make sure the header remains unchanged for the same period.
Expected Results: The header displays the correct reporting month and the delivery context stays consistent.

Test Description: Check that the report keeps the visible list ordering when no sort is changed.
Pre-Condition: The default view has more than one row in the report.
Test Steps: 1. Open the report without applying any sort. 2. Note the top few rows shown on screen. 3. Refresh the page. 4. Confirm the same row order is returned after reload. 5. Compare the first and last visible records for consistency.
Expected Results: The default ordering remains stable until the user changes the sort or filter.

Test Description: Verify Executive Summary includes renewals, expiries, and pending requests per FSD.
Pre-Condition: Report period has varied activity.
Test Steps: 1. Open register report. 2. Locate executive summary. 3. Verify renewals/expiry/pending counts. 4. Cross-check live data. 5. Export PDF.
Expected Results: Executive summary includes all FSD executive metrics.

Test Description: Verify Suppression Activity Log groups suppressions by exception entry.
Pre-Condition: Suppressions in reporting period.
Test Steps: 1. Open report. 2. Find Suppression Activity Log. 3. Verify per-entry grouping. 4. Compare audit counts. 5. Export CSV.
Expected Results: Suppression log groups by entry with counts aligned to audit.

Test Description: Verify Entries Expired This Month confirms suppression ceased and alerts resumed.
Pre-Condition: Entries expired this month.
Test Steps: 1. Open report section. 2. Review expired entries. 3. Open entry detail. 4. Confirm Expired status. 5. Run screening.
Expected Results: Section lists correct entries; screening alerts fire after expiry.

Test Description: Verify Active Exception Entries full list section shows required columns per FSD.
Pre-Condition: Report contains active entries.
Test Steps: 1. Open Exception Register report. 2. Locate Active Exception Entries section. 3. Verify columns: Customer ID, Name, Matched Watchlist Entry, Reason Code, Checker, Approval Date, Expiry Date. 4. Open sample row detail. 5. Export section.
Expected Results: Active entries section displays all FSD-required columns accurately.

Test Description: Verify Pending Requests section lists outstanding maker-checker approvals at report generation date.
Pre-Condition: Pending MC requests exist at month-end.
Test Steps: 1. Note pending request IDs before report generation. 2. Generate/open register report. 3. Locate Pending Requests section. 4. Compare listed items with MC queue. 5. Verify generation date snapshot.
Expected Results: Pending Requests section accurately reflects outstanding approvals at generation time.

Test Description: Confirm that a screening hit is suppressed only when the customer ID, watchlist scope, status, and expiry checks all pass together.
Pre-Condition: A matching CSEL entry exists for the same customer ID and the watchlist that raised the alert.
Test Steps: 1. Open a screening result that is expected to land on the exception list. 2. Check the customer ID on the alert against the ID stored in the CSEL record. 3. Verify that the watchlist shown on the alert is included in the entry scope. 4. Confirm that the entry is Active and the expiry date is still ahead of today. 5. Run the evaluation and review the final alert state.
Expected Results: The engine suppresses the hit and records a suppression event because every evaluation rule is satisfied.

Test Description: Verify that a watchlist outside the configured scope does not suppress the alert even when the customer ID matches.
Pre-Condition: An active exception exists, but the alert is triggered from a different watchlist source.
Test Steps: 1. Open a customer hit that shares the same customer ID as the exception record. 2. Read the watchlist name attached to the alert. 3. Compare it with the Watchlist Scope value stored in the CSEL entry. 4. Trigger the evaluation without changing any other alert attribute. 5. Check the result on screen and in the audit log.
Expected Results: The alert is not suppressed and continues through the normal review flow.

Test Description: Confirm that a suspended exception entry is ignored during evaluation even when the rest of the data matches.
Pre-Condition: A matching CSEL entry exists and its status is set to Suspended.
Test Steps: 1. Open an alert that would normally match the stored exception. 2. Compare the customer ID and watchlist against the suspended record. 3. Leave the alert values as they are and start the evaluation. 4. Observe the screening decision returned by the engine. 5. Review the audit trail for the same event.
Expected Results: The suspended record is skipped and the alert remains active for analyst review.

Test Description: Validate that an expired exception does not suppress a new hit after the expiry date has passed.
Pre-Condition: A valid CSEL entry exists with an expiry date in the past.
Test Steps: 1. Open the screening alert that would otherwise match the record. 2. Check the expiry date on the exception entry against the current system date. 3. Keep the alert data unchanged and rerun the evaluation. 4. Look at the final status shown for the alert. 5. Confirm whether any suppression note was written.
Expected Results: The engine treats the record as expired, so the alert is not suppressed.

Test Description: Check the boundary case where the expiry date is exactly today and no suppression should be applied.
Pre-Condition: The exception entry is Active and its expiry date is set to the current date.
Test Steps: 1. Open the matching screening hit for the same customer. 2. Review the expiry date on the CSEL entry. 3. Compare it with the current system date shown by the application. 4. Submit the evaluation as-is. 5. Confirm the alert outcome after the run.
Expected Results: The record is treated as not valid for suppression because the current date is not before the expiry date.

Test Description: Ensure that a customer ID mismatch blocks suppression even when the name and watchlist appear to match.
Pre-Condition: An active exception exists for a similar customer name but with a different customer ID.
Test Steps: 1. Open the incoming alert and note the customer ID from the case header. 2. Open the exception entry and compare its customer ID field. 3. Check that the watchlist and status values still look valid. 4. Run the evaluation without editing either record. 5. Review the final decision returned by the engine.
Expected Results: The alert is raised normally because customer ID matching is exact and the IDs do not match.

Test Description: Verify that a missing customer ID on the alert does not allow the exception to suppress the hit.
Pre-Condition: The alert is incomplete and the customer ID field is blank or unavailable.
Test Steps: 1. Open the screening hit created from incomplete customer data. 2. Check that the customer ID field is empty in the alert details. 3. Compare the remaining fields with the exception entry. 4. Run the evaluation and watch for the decision message. 5. Open the audit trail entry for the same alert.
Expected Results: The alert is not suppressed and the missing ID is treated as a failed match condition.

Test Description: Check that a blank watchlist scope on the exception record prevents suppression.
Pre-Condition: The CSEL entry exists, but the Watchlist Scope field is empty or not configured.
Test Steps: 1. Open the exception record and confirm the scope field is blank. 2. Open an incoming screening hit for the same customer ID. 3. Verify that the alert belongs to a specific watchlist source. 4. Start the evaluation using the same data set. 5. Review the alert status after processing.
Expected Results: The hit is not suppressed because the watchlist scope rule cannot be satisfied.

Test Description: Confirm that inactive or draft status records are ignored during evaluation.
Pre-Condition: The exception entry exists, but its status is not Active.
Test Steps: 1. Open the alert that should have matched the exception. 2. Check the status field on the CSEL record. 3. Make sure the customer ID and watchlist values still line up. 4. Run the evaluation with the same data in place. 5. Observe whether the alert is suppressed or escalated.
Expected Results: The engine ignores the non-active record and the alert remains unsuppressed.

Test Description: Validate that one valid exception among multiple candidate records is enough to suppress the hit.
Pre-Condition: More than one CSEL entry exists for the same customer, but only one record is fully valid.
Test Steps: 1. Open the screening case and list the candidate exception records returned by the engine. 2. Compare each record against the customer ID, watchlist scope, status, and expiry date. 3. Identify the one record that satisfies every rule. 4. Submit the evaluation again if needed so the engine can settle on the best candidate. 5. Check the final alert state and the matching record used by the system.
Expected Results: The alert is suppressed because at least one exception entry fully satisfies the evaluation criteria.

Test Description: Confirm that the suppression event is written to audit when an alert is successfully suppressed.
Pre-Condition: A matching active exception exists and the hit is expected to be suppressed.
Test Steps: 1. Open the alert that should be suppressed. 2. Run the evaluation using the matching CSEL entry. 3. Wait for the decision result to appear on the screen. 4. Open the audit trail or event history for the same case. 5. Check that the suppression action is captured with the right identifiers.
Expected Results: The suppression is logged in the audit trail with the customer ID, watchlist, and decision timestamp.

Test Description: Verify that a small spelling change still matches when the score stays above the configured threshold.
Pre-Condition: An exception entry exists with a name that is very close to the incoming alert name.
Test Steps: 1. Open a screening hit where the customer name differs by one or two characters. 2. Check the match score shown by the evaluation engine. 3. Compare the score with the threshold configured for the list. 4. Complete the evaluation and observe the decision returned to the analyst. 5. Open the linked audit event for the same comparison.
Expected Results: The fuzzy name match is accepted and the alert is suppressed when the score is at or above the threshold.

Test Description: Confirm that a name variation below the configured threshold does not apply the exception.
Pre-Condition: The incoming name is close to the stored name, but the score is expected to fall below the list threshold.
Test Steps: 1. Open the incoming alert and note the exact customer name. 2. Compare it with the name stored in the exception entry. 3. Inspect the score produced by the matching engine. 4. Keep the customer ID unchanged and rerun the evaluation. 5. Review the resulting alert status.
Expected Results: The exception is not applied because the name score is below the configured threshold.

Test Description: Check the boundary case where the match score is exactly equal to the configured threshold.
Pre-Condition: The list threshold is configured and the test data is prepared to land exactly on that value.
Test Steps: 1. Open the case with the borderline name variant. 2. Review the score displayed by the matching engine. 3. Compare the score to the configured threshold value. 4. Submit the evaluation and wait for the final decision. 5. Verify the alert state after processing.
Expected Results: The match is accepted when the score is equal to the threshold, and the hit is suppressed.

Test Description: Confirm that phonetic matching catches a sound-alike name even when the spelling is different.
Pre-Condition: The data set contains two names that sound alike but are written differently.
